brief: The AI buildout is colliding with a power grid that cannot deliver fast enough, inference is shifting to smaller nodes closer to users, and political resistance is making mega-campus data centers harder to scale, so Morgan Stanley expects a structural shift toward behind-the-meter (BTM) power and storage. It forecasts 160 GW of incremental US data center power demand from 2026-2029: 22 GW already under construction with grid access, 36 GW of available grid capacity, and 23 GW of BTM equipment already procured, leaving a 77 GW shortfall to be filled by solid-oxide fuel cells, gas engines and turbines. MS introduces a new metric, SCACP (LCOE plus the opportunity cost of idle GPUs awaiting power), ranking Bloom Energy's SOFC #1, BorgWarner's turbine generator #2 and FTAI's aeroderivative solution #3. The grid still serves large 1 GW+ training campuses. BTM targets smaller inference nodes and Commercial & Industrial demand (40 GW incremental through 2029, a $240bn/120 GW BTM equipment TAM). Storage and virtual power plants (Sunrun and Tesla dispatched 580 MW from 140,000+ batteries during a September heat wave) complement generation, while political pushback against data center build-out reinforces rather than reverses the BTM shift.
